paraphrase: A baseline set of evaluations is described as setting a minimal level of LLM safety and trustworthiness before deployment.
notes: Descriptive framing of the baseline concept.

paraphrase: LLMs should minimally be tested pre-deployment on a baseline set of five attributes.
notes: Part 3 table lists more sub-attributes than five top-level headings; count of five as stated in intro.

paraphrase: Evaluation should use a multi-faceted combined approach that checks and cross-validates results of its constituent methods.
what_is_tested: evaluation approach (combined benchmarking, red teaming, scoring)
notes: Observation/direction for future work rather than a pre-deployment duty.

paraphrase: Recommends a baseline set of pre-deployment safety and trustworthiness evaluations for LLMs, to be run irrespective of use case.
notes: Policy position of a discussion draft.

paraphrase: Says pre-deployment evaluations are a necessary step to meet a minimum safety threshold and are best done by the deploying organisation.
notes: Wording 'necessary step' is strong but the document is a draft for discussion with no operative obligations.

paraphrase: Recommends evaluating robustness using the DecodingTrust framework.
notes: Table row; no should wording inside table.

paraphrase: Recommends evaluating factuality with TruthfulQA and frameworks such as HELM, BigBench or Eleuther harness.

locator: Part 3 table, Bias: Stereotype bias, p26
paraphrase: Recommends evaluating stereotype bias with BBQ and frameworks such as HELM or BigBench.
Recommends evaluating fairness using the UCI Adult dataset and DecodingTrust.

locator: Part 3 table, Bias: Representation of subjective opinions, p26
paraphrase: Recommends evaluating representation of subjective opinions using GlobalOpinionQA and the Durmus et al. (2023) framework.

locator: Part 3 table, Bias: Capability fairness, p26
paraphrase: Recommends evaluating capability fairness using TwitterAAE and HELM.
Recommends evaluating toxicity generation using RealToxicityPrompts scored with Perspective API.

locator: Part 3 table, Data Governance: Personal data, pp26-27
paraphrase: Recommends evaluating leakage of personal data using a pre-processed Enron email dataset and DecodingTrust.

locator: Part 3 table, Data Governance: Non-personal data, p27
paraphrase: Recommends evaluating non-personal (e.g. copyrighted) data memorisation using a pre-processed HELM dataset and HELM.
notes: Description of the attribute as non-personal data is from the table label; exact explanatory wording not seen.

paraphrase: States that evaluations should ideally use contextually attuned approaches suited to the use case.
Organisations should use the listed generic benchmarks and frameworks as a minimum precautionary measure.
notes: Same passage also disclaims endorsement of the reliability of the benchmarks.

paraphrase: Deploying organisations should consider re-running the recommended evaluations after finetuning.
notes: Re-evaluation after model change, before redeployment implied but not stated.

paraphrase: Organisations should examine the tools used to decide which evaluations to re-conduct.
notes: Weak; about deciding what to re-run.

paraphrase: Such evaluations should also be conducted periodically post-deployment, especially as tools evolve.
notes: Post-deployment; included only because it extends the pre-deployment baseline. May be out of scope.

paraphrase: Additional evaluations are warranted for frontier model risks, on top of the baseline, using the latest tools and techniques.
Organisations should always ascertain whether the model they are developing may exhibit extreme (frontier) risks.
notes: Timing relative to deployment not stated.

paraphrase: Encourages organisations to minimally conduct the baseline evaluations before LLM release and deployment.
notes: Conclusion also calls the recommendations a starting point.
